title: Phase 2A: Enterprise Foundation
description:
Harden Relicta for multi-user enterprise deployment. The CLI, governance
engine, policy system, MCP apps, and AI providers are production-ready.
Phase 2A closes the remaining gaps: persistent storage for scaling beyond
single-machine file-based state, session-based authentication for the web
dashboard, OIDC/SSO integration for enterprise identity, a versioned REST
API surface with OpenAPI documentation, and an analytics persistence layer
so risk trends and team metrics survive restarts.

features.title: Session Authentication
features.description:
Implement JWT-based session authentication for the web dashboard.
The API key auth mode works; session mode returns 501 Not Implemented.
Add token issuance, validation, refresh, and revocation. Support
secure cookie transport for browser sessions.

requirements.title: Implement JWT token service
requirements.description:
Create a token service that issues signed JWTs with configurable
expiry, refresh tokens, and revocation via a deny list. Use
HMAC-SHA256 with a server-generated secret or RSA key pair.

requirements.title: Wire session auth into middleware
requirements.description:
Replace the TODO stub in auth.go session mode with real JWT
validation. Extract claims, map to roles (Admin, Approver,
Viewer), and populate request context.

requirements.title: Add login and logout API endpoints
requirements.description:
POST /api/auth/login (credentials → JWT + refresh token),
POST /api/auth/refresh (refresh → new JWT),
POST /api/auth/logout (revoke tokens).
Rate-limit login attempts.

requirements.title: Add session auth test coverage
requirements.description:
Unit tests for token service (issue, validate, refresh, revoke).
Integration tests for login flow, expired tokens, role mapping,
and rate limiting. Target 90%+ coverage on auth package.

features.title: OIDC / SSO Integration
features.description:
Add OpenID Connect provider support so enterprises can use their
existing identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) for
dashboard authentication. Map OIDC claims to Relicta roles.

requirements.title: Add OIDC provider configuration
requirements.description:
Extend DashboardAuthConfig with OIDC fields: issuer URL,
client ID, client secret, redirect URI, scopes, and claim
mappings. Support discovery via .well-known/openid-configuration.

requirements.title: Implement OIDC authorization code flow
requirements.description:
Add /api/auth/oidc/login (redirect to IdP), /api/auth/oidc/callback
(exchange code for tokens, create session). Validate ID tokens,
extract claims, map groups to roles.

requirements.title: Map OIDC claims to Relicta roles
requirements.description:
Configurable claim-to-role mapping (e.g., groups claim "relicta-admins"
→ Admin role). Support multiple IdPs with independent mappings.
Fallback to default Viewer role for unmapped users.

requirements.title: Test OIDC flows and document setup
requirements.description:
Integration tests with a mock OIDC provider. Document IdP setup
for Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace with example configs.

features.title: Database Persistence Layer
features.description:
Add PostgreSQL as an optional persistence backend alongside the
existing file-based event store. Enable horizontal scaling,
concurrent access, and queryable release history. Keep file-based
as the default for single-machine use.

requirements.title: Define persistence port interface
requirements.description:
Extract a clean port interface from the file event store adapter.
Both file-based and PostgreSQL adapters implement the same interface.
Use the repository pattern from the existing hexagonal architecture.

requirements.title: Implement PostgreSQL adapter
requirements.description:
Implement the persistence port using sqlc for type-safe query
generation with pgx as the driver. Store events in an append-only
events table with JSONB payload. Add indexes for release ID,
timestamp, and event type. Use connection pooling.

requirements.title: Add database migration framework
requirements.description:
Embed SQL migrations via go:embed. Support up/down migrations
with version tracking. Add `relicta db migrate` and
`relicta db status` CLI commands. Use golang-migrate or similar.

requirements.title: Add persistence configuration
requirements.description:
Extend config schema with persistence section: backend type
(file, postgres), connection string (with env var expansion),
pool size, migration mode (auto, manual). Wire adapter selection
in container setup.

requirements.title: Add persistence layer tests
requirements.description:
Unit tests with interface mocks. Integration tests with testcontainers
for PostgreSQL. Test migration up/down, concurrent writes, event
replay, and failover to file-based when DB is unreachable.

features.title: Analytics Persistence
features.description:
Persist risk trends, governance decisions, and team metrics so the
dashboard shows historical data across restarts. Build on the
persistence port interface from the database feature.

requirements.title: Capture analytics events
requirements.description:
Emit structured analytics events for: risk evaluations, policy
decisions, approval outcomes, release durations, bump types.
Store via the persistence port (file or PostgreSQL).

requirements.title: Add analytics query endpoints
requirements.description:
GET /api/analytics/risk-trends (time-series risk scores),
GET /api/analytics/decisions (policy decision distribution),
GET /api/analytics/team (approvals per actor, release velocity).
Support date range and granularity parameters.

requirements.title: Implement analytics aggregation
requirements.description:
Pre-aggregate metrics for dashboard performance: daily/weekly/monthly
rollups for risk scores, decision counts, release frequency.
For file backend, aggregate on read. For PostgreSQL, use
materialized views or scheduled aggregation.

requirements.title: Add analytics test coverage
requirements.description:
Unit tests for event capture and aggregation logic. Integration
tests for query endpoints with seeded data. Verify both file
and PostgreSQL backends produce consistent results.

features.title: REST API Hardening
features.description:
Version the REST API, add pagination to list endpoints, generate
OpenAPI documentation, and add structured error responses. Make
the API suitable for third-party integrations.

requirements.title: Add API versioning
requirements.description:
Prefix all API routes with /api/v1/. Add version negotiation
via Accept header. Document versioning policy (additive changes
in minor, breaking changes in major).

requirements.title: Add pagination and filtering to list endpoints
requirements.description:
Cursor-based pagination for releases, events, and audit trail
endpoints. Support limit, cursor, sort, and filter query params.
Return Link headers and pagination metadata in response body.

requirements.title: Generate OpenAPI specification
requirements.description:
Annotate handlers with OpenAPI metadata. Generate spec at build
time or serve at /api/v1/openapi.json. Include authentication
schemes, error responses, and example payloads.

requirements.title: Implement structured error responses
requirements.description:
Standardize error format: {code, message, details, request_id}.
Map domain errors to HTTP status codes consistently. Add
request ID middleware for correlation.

requirements.title: Add API contract tests
requirements.description:
Integration tests verifying pagination, error formats, versioning,
and OpenAPI spec accuracy. Use golden file tests for response
shapes. Target full endpoint coverage.

features.title: Webhook Delivery Hardening
features.description:
The webhook config schema exists but the delivery engine needs
production hardening: persistent delivery queue, retry with
backoff, delivery logging, and dead-letter handling.

requirements.title: Add persistent webhook delivery queue
requirements.description:
Queue webhook deliveries for async processing. Persist pending
deliveries so they survive restarts. Process in order per
endpoint with configurable concurrency.

requirements.title: Implement retry with exponential backoff
requirements.description:
Retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff and jitter.
Respect Retry-After headers. Move to dead-letter after max
retries. Log all delivery attempts with status codes.

requirements.title: Add webhook delivery log
requirements.description:
Log delivery attempts with timestamp, endpoint, status code,
response time, and payload hash. Expose via
GET /api/v1/webhooks/:id/deliveries. Support manual re-delivery.

requirements.title: Add webhook delivery tests
requirements.description:
Unit tests for queue, retry logic, and backoff calculation.
Integration tests with httptest server simulating failures,
slow responses, and redirects.

features.title: Monorepo Workspace Orchestration
features.description: Add first-class monorepo support for governing changes across multiple packages in a single repository. Detect workspace structure (Go modules, npm workspaces, Cargo workspaces), analyze per-package changes independently, support independent versioning per package, and coordinate cross-package releases. This addresses the PRD's "Monorepo support gaps" risk (rated High) and is critical for enterprise adoption where monorepos are standard.

features.title: CGP Protocol Wire Format
features.description: Formalize the Change Governance Protocol (CGP) wire format as described in PRD Section 17. Implement CGP message types (change.proposal, change.decision, change.execution_authorized) as structured JSON with versioning. Add CGP endpoints to the MCP server so AI agents can propose changes via the protocol. Create a CGP SDK package that other tools can import to become CGP-compliant. This positions Relicta as the reference implementation of an open governance standard.

features.title: Audience-Aware Release Communication
features.description: Implement the stakeholder communication layer from PRD Section 11. Generate audience-specific release narratives (engineering, product, executive, external) derived from approved governance decisions. Support bundling changes across components into coherent narratives. Add communication templates with configurable tone and detail level. Integrate with existing AI providers for narrative generation. This moves Relicta from "output" (changelogs) to "outcomes" (stakeholder communication).

features.title: Release Memory and Learning
features.description: Build the historical context system from PRD Section 16.4. Track past incidents, rollbacks, and their root causes. Identify patterns of risky changes across releases. Feed historical outcomes back into risk scoring so future evaluations improve over time. Store release memory in the persistence layer (file or PostgreSQL). Surface insights via the dashboard analytics. This enables Relicta to continuously improve beyond what stateless tools can achieve.

features.title: Dashboard Frontend Separation
features.description: Extract the embedded Vue dashboard into a standalone deployable frontend as described in PRD Section 14.1. Support CDN-friendly deployment (Vercel, CloudFront, S3). Add real-time updates via WebSocket for release progress, approval notifications, and analytics. Build dashboard views for the new analytics data (risk trends, decision distribution, team metrics). The Go backend serves as a standalone API service alongside the CLI.

features.title: Pre-release and Release Channel Support
features.description: Add pre-release versioning (alpha, beta, rc) and release channels (stable, canary, next). Support promoting pre-releases through channels with governance gates at each stage. Track channel-specific policies (e.g., canary requires lower approval threshold than stable). This addresses the PRD's "Missing critical workflows (pre-release)" gap identified in the product strategy review.

features.title: Multi-Repository Governance
features.description: Coordinate release governance across multiple separate repositories that form a product or platform. Define repository groups with dependency relationships, synchronize version constraints across repos, enforce cross-repo release policies (e.g., "service-api must release before service-client"), and provide a unified view of multi-repo release state. Support both centralized governance (one Relicta instance governs all repos) and federated governance (each repo has Relicta, coordinated via CGP messages). Integrate with the existing CGP protocol for cross-repo proposal/decision exchange.

features.title: Runtime Observability Integration
features.description: Connect post-deployment outcomes back to the release memory system for continuous learning. Integrate with observability platforms (Prometheus, Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry) to automatically detect incidents, error rate spikes, and rollbacks that correlate with specific releases. Auto-record outcomes in the release memory when deployment metrics cross configured thresholds. Surface deployment health in the dashboard with release-correlated metrics. This closes the feedback loop so Relicta's risk scoring improves with real production data rather than relying solely on code analysis.

features.title: EU AI Act Article 12 Evidence Pack
features.description: Extend `relicta report --type` to emit `eu-ai-act-article-12` log bundle from existing CGP audit chain. Maps governance events to Article 12 logging requirements: start/end timestamps per use, reference databases, input data leading to match, identification of natural persons verifying results. Output formats: JSON Lines (machine), Markdown summary (auditor), CSV (regulator). Retention metadata: 6-month minimum log retention enforced via persistence layer config. Files to extend: `internal/cli/report.go`, `internal/compliance/report.go`, `internal/compliance/article12.go` (new). Source: hash-chained audit at `internal/cgp/audit/`. Forcing function: August 2026 EU AI Act high-risk provisions.

features.title: EU AI Act Annex IV Technical Documentation Generator
features.description: New `relicta report --type ai-act-annex-iv` produces section-by-section Annex IV technical documentation from CGP risk + audit + memory data. Sections: general description, detailed description of system elements, monitoring/functioning/control, risk management system (maps to risk calculator output), data and data governance (maps to actor attribution), accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity (maps to attestation chain), human oversight (maps to approval records). Output: Markdown + PDF. 10-year retention metadata. This is the differentiator Microsoft AGT does not generate. Files: `internal/compliance/annex_iv.go` (new), templates in `internal/compliance/templates/annex_iv/`. Required for €60-80K fintech/healthtech buyer in EU.

features.title: Agent Autonomy Profiles (per-actor governance budgets)
features.description: Extend `internal/cgp/policy/` with `actor_budget.go` defining per-actor budgets: max_blast_radius, max_risk_score, max_dollar_cost_usd, requires_cosign list, allowed_tools/denied_tools whitelist, time-window limits. Schema in `.relicta/actor-budgets.yaml` keyed on actor_type + actor_id glob. Enforcement at `internal/mcp/server.go` tool dispatch — pre-flight checks resolve actor from MCP session metadata, reject with structured error if violated. Extend `ActorType` enum at `internal/domain/release/domain/run.go:49` with ActorID string. Audit chain records every budget check. Default profile: refuse `--yes` on agent-actor + risk>=0.4 + no policy file. Killer differentiator over GitHub Required Reviewers (no actor-typed concept) and Microsoft AGT (runtime, not release).

features.title: Security Gate Hardening
features.description: Remove `|| true` from `Makefile:520-525` security-scan target. Run `nox baseline_add` against current 280 findings (1 critical, 170 high, 100 medium, 11 low) — triage and either fix or baseline with justification. SEC-435 (.env.example, docs) likely false positive — baseline with rationale. SEC-436/437 in `internal/errors/errors.go:475-477` need real review (error message disclosure?). AI-007 already baselined. Add `make security-scan-strict` to `check-ci` as failing target. CI gate: zero NEW high+ findings on PR. Non-negotiable for any regulated-buyer demo.

features.title: CLAUDE.md Reality Sync
features.description: Fix architecture documentation drift in both repos. CLI: `relicta/CLAUDE.md` claims `internal/state/` (does not exist), claims `internal/service/{git,version,ai,template}` (actually under `internal/infrastructure/`). Update to reflect 23 real internal dirs: analysis, analytics, application, benchmark, cgp, cli, compliance, config, container, domain, errors, fileutil, httpserver, infrastructure, mcp, observability, plugin, security, service, ui, version. Hub: `relicta-hub/CLAUDE.md` claims stdlib `net/http` routing (uses Gin), claims "Hub imports domain logic from CLI" (zero CLI imports verified). Replace with honest description of skeleton state + alpha banner. Trust leak in enterprise security review until fixed.

features.title: Vanta API Integration (Evidence Push)
features.description: Push Relicta attestation events to Vanta as evidence artifacts via Vanta REST API. New plugin `plugins/vanta/` (Go, gRPC plugin pattern matching existing plugin architecture). Triggered on PostPublish hook. Maps Relicta events to Vanta evidence types: governance decisions → custom evidence, audit chain entries → control evidence, actor attestations → access reviews. Configurable framework mapping (SOC2 CC6.1/CC7.1/CC7.4 already in `enterprise-soc2` template). Vanta released MCP server April 15 2026 — explicit partnership angle, not competitive. Sarah persona: "Vanta partnership = non-negotiable." Files: `plugins/vanta/main.go`, `plugins/vanta/client.go`, `plugins/vanta/mapping.go`. Drata follows same pattern as P1.

features.title: Plugin Registry Cull
features.description: `plugins/registry.yaml` lists 39 named plugins (github, gitlab, slack, jira, npm, homebrew, docker, etc.) but `plugins/` has zero `.go` files — each entry references separate repo. Most likely don't exist. Security review red flag: every empty plugin = credibility leak. Cull registry to 5-7 plugins actually owned, tested, and shipped (recommended: github, gitlab, slack, jira, npm). Remove other 32+ entries. Add `make plugin-verify` target validating each registry entry resolves to working binary at advertised checksum. Alternative: keep registry but mark unverified entries as `status: community` with disclaimer. Position decision: "registry of vapor" vs "small registry of real" — pick small/real.

features.title: Reposition README and Tagline
features.description: Rewrite README hero from "The governance layer for software change" (vague, overlaps Vanta+MS AGT) to "Cryptographically-attested release governance for AI-native engineering. EU AI Act Annex IV ready." Differentiator stack: (1) hash-chained audit chain (CGP) 99.1% test coverage, (2) actor-typed governance Human/CI/Agent, (3) Article 12 + Annex IV from existing audit data (Microsoft AGT does not), (4) pushes evidence to Vanta/Drata (partner not replace). Add comparison matrix vs Vanta (different surface: ex-ante decision attestation vs ex-post posture scan), Microsoft AGT (release-time vs runtime), GitHub Required Reviewers (gate vs prove). Update brand assets reference. Files: `README.md`, `docs/positioning.md` (new).

features.title: AI 2026 Model Migration
features.description: Bump default models from 2024-vintage to 2026 across providers. Anthropic at `anthropic.go:27`: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` → `claude-sonnet-4-6` default, `claude-opus-4-7` for high-stakes release narratives, `claude-haiku-4-5` for diff summaries. OpenAI at `service.go:138`: `gpt-4` → `gpt-5` default, `gpt-5-mini` for narrative. Gemini at `gemini.go:26`: `gemini-2.0-flash-exp` → `gemini-2.5-flash`. Add per-use-case override config: `ai.model_overrides.{release_notes, risk_narrative, communicate, summarize_diff}`. Add `WithModel(string)` option in `service.go`. Update `docs/ai-providers.md` table (currently cites GPT-4o/3.5, Claude 3.5 Sonnet/3 Opus, Gemini 2.0 Flash/1.5 Pro — all pre-2026). Risk: prompts tuned for old models may regress — gate bump on eval harness V0.

features.title: Anthropic Prompt Caching
features.description: Implement `cache_control: ephemeral` blocks on Anthropic API calls. Currently zero `cache_control` hits in `internal/` and `pkg/`. Prime targets: long stable system prompts in `internal/infrastructure/ai/prompts.go` (281 LOC), repo context blocks (commit list, file globs, codebase summary) re-tokenized every release. Expected impact: 5-10x cost reduction on repeated governance evaluations + release-notes path. Cache key strategy: hash repo context block, invalidate on detected schema change. Files to extend: `internal/infrastructure/ai/anthropic.go`, `internal/infrastructure/ai/prompts.go`. Cost discipline = enterprise procurement requirement.

features.title: Structured Outputs and JSON Schema Mode
features.description: Replace regex-parsing of LLM output with provider-native structured outputs. Currently zero `response_format`/`ResponseFormat` hits across codebase. OpenAI: `response_format: json_schema` with strict mode for `GovernanceDecision`, `RiskNarrative`, `ReleaseNotes`, `AudienceNarrative` types. Anthropic: tool-use with structured output schema. Define schemas in `internal/infrastructure/ai/schemas/`. Eliminates parse failures and "model returned malformed JSON" runtime errors that LLM-as-content-generator-for-governance cannot tolerate. Files: `openai.go`, `anthropic.go`, `gemini.go`, new `schemas/` dir. Reliability requirement for governance product.

features.title: AI Eval Harness V0
features.description: Build LLM evaluation harness — currently absent. New `internal/infrastructure/ai/evals/`. 150 golden YAML examples across categories: release-notes (60), risk-narrative (40), communicate-cmd (30), diff-summary (20). Each: input, context, rubric (factuality, governance-alignment, terseness, no-hallucination, structured-output-valid), optional reference. Judge model: `claude-opus-4-7` LLM-as-judge with structured output (1-5 per criterion + rationale). Cross-check 10% with `gpt-5` for judge bias. CI gate `make ai-eval`: fail if mean < 4.0 or factuality < 3 or structured-output-valid < 5. Run on AI-touching PRs only via path filter. Cost ~$2/full run. Files: `evals/runner.go`, `evals/judge.go`, `evals/golden/*.yaml`, `.github/workflows/ai-eval.yml`. **Blocks model bump merges.** Non-negotiable for governance-grade AI prose.

features.title: Postgres Adapter Test Coverage 0% to 70%
features.description: `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/` ships at 0.0% test coverage. `store.go` 294, `migrator.go` 308, `pool.go` 32 — all untested. README claims "PostgreSQL persistence" — claim becomes true at 70%+ coverage. Add `testcontainers-go` integration suite. Test scenarios: connection pool lifecycle, migration up/down idempotency, concurrent writes (event store), failover to file-based when DB unreachable, transaction isolation, JSONB query correctness. Add migrations 002-005 covering aggregates beyond events (releases, approvals, audit_chain projections, attestations). Single events table with JSONB without projections is event-store-as-database antipattern. Block release until coverage gate.

features.title: Reverse MCP Resources (governance-as-context)
features.description: MCP server at `internal/mcp/server.go` (2362 LOC) exposes governance tools to AI agents. Add MCP resources (readable context, complement to tools) so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Devin) plan WITH governance context — shift-left from post-facto governance. Resources to expose: `relicta://policy/current` (active CGP policy as JSON), `relicta://risk-budget/{actor_id}` (remaining budget), `relicta://recent-incidents?days=30` (postmortem feed), `relicta://blast-radius/{service}` (dependency/impact graph), `relicta://release-history/{service}?limit=10` (prior runs + outcomes), `relicta://compliance-frameworks` (active frameworks). Verify first whether `resources/list` handler exists in `server.go`; if absent, add. Turns Relicta into context provider for any MCP-aware coding agent. Differentiation moat against Vanta MCP (different scope: compliance posture vs governance context).

features.title: Drata API Integration (Evidence Push)
features.description: Mirror Vanta integration for Drata. New plugin `plugins/drata/`. Drata API focused on extracting compliance data and programmatically uploading evidence types. Push Relicta attestations as evidence artifacts. Drata 170+ integrations covers AWS/GitHub/Okta/Workspace — Relicta becomes upstream provenance source for AI-attributed releases that Drata cannot generate from CI/Git data alone. Same gRPC plugin architecture as Vanta plugin. Files: `plugins/drata/main.go`, `plugins/drata/client.go`, `plugins/drata/mapping.go`. Sequencing: ship after Vanta validates pattern.

features.title: Cobra Command Groups
features.description: 30+ flat top-level commands violate Hick's + Miller's 7±2. `relicta --help` is wall of unstructured commands. Use `cobra.Group` (Cobra 1.6+) to organize. Group IDs: `lifecycle` (init/plan/bump/notes/approve/publish/release/promote/rollback/cancel), `inspect` (status/blast/history/evaluate/report), `multi` (group/* multirepo), `extend` (plugin*/mcp/serve/server), `ops` (db/health/metrics/clean/verify). Set `cmd.GroupID` on every `AddCommand` in `internal/cli/root.go`. Zero behavior change, ~40 LOC. XS effort, high UX leverage.

features.title: Approval Card Shared Schema
features.description: Three approval surfaces drift: TUI (`internal/cli/approve.go:469-510` tabwriter plain text), web (`web/src/views/ApprovalWorkflow.vue`), MCP server tool dispatch. Risk score formatted three ways. Define `ApprovalCardSchema` JSON contract in `internal/governance/` (or `pkg/cgp/approval_card.go`). Generate Vue prop types via `openapi-typescript` from the schema. Mirror lipgloss render in TUI from same struct. Single source of truth for: risk score, factors list, diff summary, actor, required actions ordering, rationale display. Jakob's Law banked across surfaces. Files: schema definition, TUI renderer extraction, Vue component refactor.

features.title: Risk Display lipgloss Visualization
features.description: `internal/cli/approve.go:455-511` displays risk as plain `Risk Score: 47.0% (MEDIUM)` text alongside other fields in tabwriter. Highest-leverage decision input given lowest visual weight. Charmbracelet lipgloss already imported. Render risk: bordered lipgloss block, `lipgloss.Color("196"/"214"/"34")` for HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, horizontal `progress.Model` bar, top-3 risk factors above release metadata. APCA-compliant pairs with `▲▲▲` glyph for color-blind / `NO_COLOR` env. Same struct exposed via Approval Card Schema for web consumption (see related feature). Files: `internal/cli/approve.go`, new `internal/ui/risk.go` for reusable component.

features.title: Init Quick Mode
features.description: Current `relicta init` 8-step wizard violates Goal-Gradient + Doherty Threshold. New `relicta init --quick` infers from git remote + `package.json`/`go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` → 1-confirm screen with detected defaults. Existing wizard becomes `relicta init --guided`. Show progress `[3/8]` via `progress.Model`. Collapse advanced (channels, OIDC, plugins) behind `--advanced` flag. Init wizard should also write a starter governance policy file by default (sensible: require approval for major, auto-approve patch <0.3 risk, block on security factors) — first governed release achievable without policy authoring. Files: `internal/cli/init.go`, `internal/config/templates/`.

features.title: policy.go God File Split
features.description: `internal/cli/policy.go` is 2318 LOC with 57 functions mixing validate/list/scaffold/test/matrix/explain. Highest contributor-friction file in repo. Split by verb into 6 files: `policy_validate.go`, `policy_list.go`, `policy_scaffold.go`, `policy_test.go`, `policy_matrix.go`, `policy_explain.go`. Each delegates to existing `internal/application/policy/` (already exists, underused). Same pattern for `internal/mcp/server.go` (2362 LOC) — split by tool category. Domain layer is clean — don't touch what works. PR review time drops from hours to minutes. Unblocks parallel feature work. Plan/approve/release CLI files (under 1100 LOC each) tolerable for now — defer.

features.title: Architecture Fitness Functions
features.description: Zero fitness/architecture tests. `find . -name 'arch_test.go'` empty. Add two as priority. **FF#1 Hexagonal boundary** at `internal/architecture/layering_test.go`: assert packages under `internal/cli/` MUST NOT import `internal/infrastructure/*` except via `internal/application/*`. Tool: `go list -deps -json ./internal/cli/...` filtered. Catches policy.go-style rot at PR time. **FF#2 CGP protocol stability** at `pkg/cgp/compat_test.go`: assert golden JSON envelopes from `testdata/v0.1/*.json` MUST round-trip through current Marshal/Unmarshal byte-identical. `//go:embed testdata`, deep-equal. Protects external CGP consumers from silent breakage — critical because CGP positioned as protocol with public SDK.

features.title: Web Dashboard Accessibility CI Gate
features.description: Web dashboard at `relicta/web/` has 11 Vue views shipped, a11y unverified. Tailwind defaults rarely hit AAA contrast on risk colors (red/amber/green = APCA failure pattern). Risk pages = highest stakes. Compliance/Security Officer persona uses screen readers in regulated industries — literal target buyer. Add `@axe-core/playwright` to existing test setup. CI gate: zero violations on `ApprovalWorkflow.vue`, `ReleaseDetail.vue`, `GovernanceAnalytics.vue`. Replace red/green-only state encoding with APCA-compliant pair + redundant icon (shape+color). Add `aria-live="polite"` on approval state changes. Files: `web/playwright.config.ts`, `web/tests/a11y/*.spec.ts`, audit pass on Vue components.

features.title: Plugin Sandbox Honesty
features.description: `internal/plugin/sandbox/sandbox_darwin.go:14-28` self-documents that RLIMIT_AS unenforced on Apple Silicon, no `sandbox-exec` profile, CPU limits absent. README markets sandboxing as security boundary. Two paths: (a) ship `sandbox-exec` profile generation on darwin + seccomp-bpf on linux + plugin signature verification (currently missing entirely from `manager.go`), or (b) downgrade marketing — rename to `ResourceAdvisor`, surface "best-effort" loudly at config-load time, require explicit `--allow-untrusted-plugins` flag for non-signed plugins. Pick (a) for enterprise credibility OR (b) for honest minimal viable. Either way: honesty before next major release.

features.title: CGP Protocol Wire Format
features.description: Formalize the Change Governance Protocol (CGP) wire format as structured JSON with versioning. Implement CGP message types (change.proposal, change.decision, change.execution_authorized). Add CGP endpoints to the MCP server. Create CGP SDK package (pkg/cgp) for other tools to become CGP-compliant.

features.title: Audience-Aware Release Communication
features.description: Generate audience-specific release narratives (engineering, product, executive, external) derived from approved governance decisions. Support bundling changes across components into coherent narratives. Add communication templates with configurable tone and detail level. Integrate with existing AI providers for narrative generation.

features.title: Release Memory with Mnemos Integration
features.description: Build historical context system using Mnemos as optional memory backend. Track past incidents, rollbacks, and root causes. Identify patterns of risky changes across releases. Feed historical outcomes back into risk scoring. Support file-based (default) and Mnemos HTTP API backends.

features.title: Learning with Chronos Pattern Detection
features.description: Integrate Chronos for time-series pattern detection on release metrics. Detect trends, spikes, stalls, anomalies in risk scores, deployment frequency, CFR, MTTR. Feed Chronos signals back into risk scoring for continuous improvement. Support multiple backends (memory, SQLite, PostgreSQL).

features.title: Consolidate the two file-based release repositories
features.description:
There are two independent file-based implementations of the ReleaseRun aggregate, with incompatible on-disk schemas, and commands disagree about which to use.

WHAT THEY ARE

1. internal/domain/release/adapters/FileReleaseRunRepository — wired by internal/domain/release/factory.go:60 and used by the release services (plan, bump, notes, approve, publish) and by `relicta status`. Writes the changeset at the top level of the run JSON and restores it on load.

2. internal/infrastructure/persistence/FileReleaseRepository — wired at internal/container/container.go:169, returned by app.ReleaseRepository(), and used by the governance paths. Expects the changeset nested under plan.changeset, and reconstructs runs lossily.

THE CONSEQUENCE, OBSERVED

`relicta evaluate` failed on every release, in every repository, with:

  governance evaluation failed: failed to evaluate proposal: invalid proposal:
  invalid scope: either commitRange or commits is required

`plan` wrote the run with (1); `evaluate` read it with (2); (2) found no changeset because it looks in a different place, so governance had no commit range and refused the proposal. A core command — the one that computes the risk score and policy verdict the product is built around — could not succeed at all.

WHAT (2) LOSES ON LOAD (internal/infrastructure/persistence/release_repository.go:739-741)

  BaseRef  <- dto.Branch      (the branch, not the base ref)
  HeadSHA  <- ""              (empty)
  Commits  <- nil             (dropped)
  ChangeSet                   (not found: different schema location)

So a run loaded through (2) cannot support anything that needs commits, HEAD, or the base ref — which is most of governance.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION ALREADY LANDED

getLatestReleaseForEvaluate now loads through the release services' repository, the same one status reads and plan wrote. That makes evaluate work without touching the duplication. It is a redirect, not a fix: app.ReleaseRepository() still returns the lossy implementation and other callers still use it.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE

- app.ReleaseRepository() has other callers that would need auditing for the same class of bug
- the two schemas differ, so consolidating means deciding whether to migrate existing .relicta/releases/*.json or read both shapes during a transition
- domainrelease.Repository and ports.ReleaseRunRepository are different interfaces over the same concept, so consolidation is an interface decision as well as an implementation one
- publish and approve both take governance paths that would change behaviour

SUGGESTED APPROACH

1. Inventory every caller of app.ReleaseRepository() and record which are affected by the lossy load
2. Decide the single owning implementation — (1) is the better candidate: it is the writer, it round-trips the changeset, and the release services already depend on it
3. Give the surviving type the union of the two interfaces, or narrow callers to the interface they actually need
4. Handle existing on-disk runs: either read both schema shapes for a release or two, or migrate on load
5. Delete the loser, and add a test that a run written by the release services round-trips with commits, HEAD SHA, base ref and changeset intact — the absence of that test is why this survived

ACCEPTANCE

One implementation. A round-trip test proving commits, head_sha, base_ref and changeset all survive save/load. evaluate, approve and publish all read runs through it.

features.title: Make versioning.tag_prefix work for non-"v" prefixes
features.description:
Tracked on GitHub as relicta-tech/relicta#231; logged here so it stays in the backlog.

versioning.tag_prefix is configurable, TagList.FilterByPrefix exists, and monorepo docs describe app-v1.2.3 style tags. But a tag with any prefix other than "v" is never recognised as a version tag, so the setting has no effect beyond its default.

CAUSE

sourcecontrol.NewTag (internal/domain/sourcecontrol/tag.go:23) decides version-ness by parsing the whole tag name, and version.Parse accepts only bare semver or a leading "v":

  Parse("1.5.0")         -> 1.5.0
  Parse("v1.5.0")        -> 1.5.0
  Parse("release-1.5.0") -> invalid semantic version
  Parse("rel/1.5.0")     -> invalid semantic version
  Parse("app-v1.5.0")    -> invalid semantic version

Such tags are dropped by TagList.VersionTags() BEFORE FilterByPrefix can be applied — the usual call order is FilterByPrefix(prefix).VersionTags(), and the second step discards what the first selected.

CONSEQUENCES for any project not using "v"

- plan cannot find the previous version tag, so it computes a baseline of "no previous release" and a changeset spanning the whole history
- status cannot detect that a release happened since a run was planned
- monorepo-style prefixes do not work at all, though app-v1.2.3 is the documented pattern for blast and workspace versioning

The failure is silent: nothing reports that the prefix was ignored, so the project simply appears to have no releases.

RELATED

internal/domain/release/app/plan.go:131 separately hardcodes the prefix:

  tag, err := uc.repoInspector.GetLatestVersionTag(ctx, "v")

even though cfg.Versioning.TagPrefix is threaded into the CLI's AnalyzeInput elsewhere. Both need fixing; that line alone would still hit the parse limitation.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION FIRST

The right shape depends on what a monorepo tag is meant to be: "prefix app-v plus semver", or a component-qualified tag with its own type carrying component and version separately. blast and workspace versioning both depend on the answer, so deciding that comes before implementing.

SUGGESTED APPROACH

1. Decide the monorepo tag model (plain prefix vs component-qualified type)
2. Teach the tag domain to strip a configured prefix before parsing, or add a prefix-aware constructor
3. Pass cfg.Versioning.TagPrefix in plan.go instead of "v"
4. Revisit detectRunStaleness in internal/cli/status.go, which currently cannot see non-"v" releases

EXISTING TEST

TestDetectRunStaleness_NonVTagPrefixesAreNotDetected (internal/cli/status_staleness_test.go) pins the current behavior and FAILS once this is fixed, as a prompt to revisit the staleness detector at the same time.

features.title: Decide what relicta init should write, and make error messages match
features.description:
`relicta init` writes 6 of the schema's 21 top-level config sections, so error messages that tell a user to edit a setting frequently name a key the generated file does not contain.

WRITTEN: versioning, changelog, ai, plugins, workflow, output

MISSING: attestation, channels, chronos, communication, dashboard, git, governance, mnemos, monorepo, observability, persistence, plugin_security, repository_groups, telemetry, webhooks

MESSAGES THAT POINT AT ABSENT KEYS

  internal/cli/evaluate.go   "enable governance in .relicta.yaml"        (governance absent)
  internal/cli/multirepo.go  "defined in .relicta.yaml under 'repository_groups'"  (absent)
  internal/cli/serve.go      "configure api_keys in .relicta.yaml"       (dashboard absent)

A user follows the instruction, opens the file, and the section is not there — with no indication of the nesting to add.

MITIGATION ALREADY LANDED

The governance case now returns errGovernanceDisabled (internal/cli/governance_disabled.go), which prints the YAML to add rather than naming a key:

  Add this to .relicta.yaml:

    governance:
      enabled: true

Verified end to end: adding exactly that makes `relicta evaluate` work. The multirepo and dashboard messages have not been given the same treatment.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS

Writing all 21 sections would produce a file of several hundred lines, most of it advanced settings at their defaults, which is its own usability problem — the current 99-line output is readable and the annotations for the dangerous settings stand out. Three plausible answers:

1. Keep a curated subset, and require every "configure X in .relicta.yaml" message to carry its own YAML snippet. Cheapest, keeps the file readable, puts the burden on error messages.
2. Write all sections, with comments, and accept the length. Most discoverable, worst to read.
3. Write the curated subset plus a commented-out block for each remaining section, so the shape is discoverable without being active. Middle ground; the annotation mechanism in internal/config/loader.go could be extended to emit these.

Whichever is chosen, the invariant worth enforcing with a test is: no user-facing message names a config key unless that key (or a commented example of it) appears in what init writes.

SUGGESTED APPROACH

1. Pick 1, 2 or 3
2. If 1: audit every message mentioning .relicta.yaml and give it a snippet, following errGovernanceDisabled
3. Add a test that scans CLI strings for ".relicta.yaml" references and checks the named section appears in WriteDefaultConfig output
4. Consider whether governance in particular deserves to be written regardless, since it gates the risk scoring the product is built around and is the section users most need to find

features.title: Wire or withdraw the cgp_* MCP tools
features.description:
The three CGP protocol tools are advertised in tools/list and cannot work. An agent enumerates them, calls one, and gets a failure on every attempt.

  cgp_propose
  cgp_authorize
  cgp_status

CAUSE

handleCGP* calls ensureCGPService (internal/mcp/server.go:708), which needs either s.cgpService or s.evaluator. `relicta mcp serve` wires neither: WithCGPService and WithEvaluator are both defined and called only from tests. So ensureCGPService always takes its error path.

Found by sweeping for option constructors that are never called in production — the same pattern as WithAdapterRepo, WithSkipPush and FindByPlanHash. Of 87 With* constructors in the tree, 40 are never called outside tests; most of those are legitimate test seams, these are not.

MITIGATION ALREADY LANDED

The failure now returns a ToolInputError explaining that no evaluator is configured and pointing at relicta_evaluate, instead of the redacted "internal error" an agent used to receive. The tools still do not work.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS

Supplying `evaluator.New()` in createMCPServer would make the tools respond, and that is what the tests do. But a bare evaluator is not the same as the CLI's governance service: the container builds that from cfg.Governance — thresholds, policies, freeze periods, trusted actors, reputation. An agent evaluating a proposal through cgp_* would get a different verdict than a human running `relicta evaluate` on the same change, which for a governance tool is worse than the tool being absent.

Three options:

1. Expose the container's configured evaluator (or the governance service's) and wire that. Correct, and makes agent and CLI agree. Needs an accessor the container does not currently have, and a decision about whether the CGP protocol path should share governance's configuration or have its own.

2. Withdraw the three tools from tools/list until they can be wired. Honest, and stops agents wasting calls. Loses the CGP protocol surface, which pkg/cgp exists to expose.

3. Keep them advertised but make the unconfigured response a documented, structured "not available here" that an agent can branch on. Cheapest; currently implemented as an isError, which is close.

Option 1 is the real answer if the CGP protocol surface is meant to be part of the product. Option 2 is right if it is not.

ACCEPTANCE

Either the three tools return real results computed with the same configuration the CLI uses, or they are not advertised. A test should assert whichever is chosen, since the current state — advertised and non-functional — is what nothing was checking.

RELATED

Other Server options never wired by `relicta mcp serve`: WithReleaseRepository, WithPolicyEngine, WithActorBudgets, WithRiskCalculator, WithCache, WithCacheDisabled. WithRiskCalculator in particular gates the fallback risk path in handleEvaluate, which therefore cannot run either. Each needs the same question asked: wire it, or remove the option and the code that depends on it.

constraints.description: File-based persistence remains the default. PostgreSQL is opt-in via config.
Existing file-based deployments must continue working without migration.
Use sqlc for type-safe query generation against PostgreSQL. No ORM dependencies.
Existing API key auth and unversioned endpoints continue working during transition.
PostgreSQL driver is included in the binary. No external runtime dependencies beyond the database itself.
All new packages must meet 80%+ test coverage before merge.
